result.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
result.summary: Fine-tuning enables safety-aligned code language models to adapt to diverse downstream tasks. However, training on untrusted data can severely undermine their ability to refuse harmful requests. Notably, we find that models comply with harmful requests even though harmfulness information remains highly decodable from their internal representations. Moreover, an initial preference for refusal does not necessarily translate into sustained refusal behavior throughout generation. Together, these findings reveal a critical gap between recognizing harmful requests and consistently refusing to fulfill them. To address this gap, we introduce SAFEHOLD, a novel provider-enforced defense framework that preserves safety alignment during harmful fine-tuning by treating refusal as a sustained generation process rather than a single response decision. Specifically, SAFEHOLD preserves the aligned model's full-vocabulary response distribution at the initial generation position through decision-boundary anchoring, while supervising the complete refusal sequence through refusal-path reinforcement. We conduct extensive experiments evaluating safety, utility, and internal mechanisms. SAFEHOLD reduces average ASR by 72.03 percentage points relative to undefended fine-tuning, outperforming five SOTA defenses by 24.32 to 70.87 percentage points. Meanwhile, it improves average HumanEval pass@1 by 10.24 percentage points over undefended fine-tuning, while maintaining an average XSTest over-refusal rate of only 2.73 percent. Overall, these results demonstrate that SAFEHOLD effectively mitigates safety degradation during harmful fine-tuning while preserving benign-task utility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究有害微调下代码模型拒答能力退化的问题，发现危害信息仍可从内部表示中解码却未转化为持续拒答行为，并提出 SAFEHOLD：在首个生成位置锚定对齐模型的完整词表分布，并对整条拒答序列做路径强化监督。
AI.relevance_reason: 「内部表示可解码但生成行为不跟随」的表示—行为落差，以及把拒答视为持续生成过程而非单点决策、对整条轨迹施加监督，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否真被答案使用、以及轨迹级贡献分配与停止决策；但无视觉或多模态成分，迁移属推测。
